input.quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
input.rationale: Section 7 is headed "Indemnification of Contractor" but its three subsections contain only liability caps (7(a)), a consequential damages waiver (7(b)) and an attorneys' fees waiver (7(c)); a document-wide search for "indemn", "hold harmless" and "defend" returns no operative indemnity language anywhere. Contractor's IP non-infringement warranty in Section 5(c) is not backed by any defence or indemnity obligation, so Clear Capital bears the cost of third-party infringement claims, Contractor-caused data breaches and Contractor's misconduct. This is the walk-away scenario (no Vendor IP indemnity at all), so we insert the playbook Vendor indemnity as new Section 7(d), with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and a carve-out from the Section 7 caps. No Customer indemnity exists that needs narrowing.

proposal.summary: Insert Contractor (Vendor) indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard defence procedure and carve-out from the liability cap.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 is headed "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains no indemnity at all, so we have added the Contractor indemnity our playbook requires for third-party IP infringement claims, Contractor's breach of law, Contractor-caused compromise of Company data, and Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, together with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure and a carve-out from the Section 7(a) cap. If you cannot accept an uncapped indemnity, we can discuss customary IP exclusions (Company modifications, combinations and specifications), the usual procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and a super-cap of 3x annual fees.

ops.text: (d) INDEMNIFICATION BY CONTRACTOR. Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services or the Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company's Confidential Information or data caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall give Contractor prompt written notice of the claim, Contractor shall have control of the defense and settlement (provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or admission on Company shall be made without Company's prior written consent), and Company shall provide reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense. Contractor's obligations under this Section 7(d) are not subject to the limitations set forth in Sections 7(a), 7(b) and 7(c).
